texts.preamble: Korada Tarakesh vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh on 7 January, 2020 Author: G.Shyam Prasad Bench: G.Shyam Prasad Hon'Ble Sri Justice G.Shyam Prasad Criminal Petition No. 7102 of 2019 Order:
texts.facts: This petition is filed under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (for short, 'the Cr.P.C.'), seeking to quash the proceedings in FIR No.136 of 2019 on the file of the Station House Officer, I Town Police Station, Srikakulam, against the petitioner / accused. 2. The brief facts of the case of prosecution are that on 29.09.2019 on reliable information, the police along with the staff and mediators visited the scene of offence, Kaki Veedhi near Amma Nanna Shop at Srikakulam and on search, they found four persons possession of four plastic bags trying to take into inside the shop and then the police caught and enquired in the presence of mediators and drafted a mediator report. The police registered a case in crime No.136/2019 on the file of the Station House Officer, I Town Police Station, Srikakulam, for the offences punishable under Sections 270, 273, 328 r/w.34 IPC and Sections 20(2) and 22(b) of COTPA Act. 3. The provisions under Sections 270 I.P.C deals with malignant act likely to spread infection of disease dangerous to life. Section 273 I.P.C deals with sale of noxious food or drink. 4. The petitioner herein is arrayed as A-1 in the above crime for the offences punishable under Sections 270, 273, 328 r/w.34 IPC and Sections 20(2) and 22(b) of COTPA Act.
texts.arguments: Learned counsel for the petitioner placing reliance on the judgments of this Court in Crl.P.No.6036 of 2019 and Crl.P.No.5421 of 2019 and batch, submits that the police are not authorized to register crime, investigate the same, and file a charge sheet against the accused in respect of tobacco products, as the tobacco products would not fall within the purview of Indian Penal Code. 7. Learned counsel for the petitioner has placed reliance on the earlier judgment of this Court in Crl.P.Nos.3731 of 2018 and batch and submits that this Court has taken a view in respect of Section 270 I.P.C as held in unnumbered Paragraph which reads as under: Korada Tarakesh vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh on 7 January, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56391879/ 1 "According to Section 33 of I.P.C, the word 'act' denotes as well a series of acts as a single act; the work 'omission' denotes as well a series of omissions as a single omission. Thus, it means, anything done by any of the persons. Transportation of Khaini, Pan Masala or chewing tobacco itself would not spread any infection or disease and if the khaini is chewed, it may cause danger to health of any individual, but transportation will not spread any infection or disease dangerous to health. Therefore, the allegations made in the complaint i.e. transportation of chewing tobacco or Khaini or Pan Masala also do not constitute an offence punishable under Section 270 of I.P.C. 8. It is appropriate to refer to the provisions of Section 270 I.P.C, which reads as under: "According to section 270 of Indian penal code, Whoever malignantly does any act which is, and which he knows or has reason to believe to be, likely to spread the infection of any disease dangerous to life, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both". 9. 10. Section 273 IPC deals with sale of noxious food or drink, which reads as under: "According to section 273 of Indian penal code, Whoever sells, or offers or exposes for sale, as food or drink, any article which has been rendered or has become noxious, or is in a state unfit for food or drink, knowing or having reason to believe that the same is noxious as food or drink, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both". 11. 'Transportation' of such noxious food is not included in the offence punishable under Section 273 of I.P.C, only few acts were included i.e., sale of noxious food or drink is Korada Tarakesh vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh on 7 January, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56391879/ 2 an offence. 12. Learned counsel further submits that the police are not competent to take cognizance for the offences punishable under Sections 270 and 273 IPC, as there is special enactment in respect of the products seized in this case covered under COTPA Act. 13. The Food, Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (for short 'FSS Act'), Section 41 deals with the power to warrant and authorization, 42 deals with power of entry, search, seizure and arrest without warrant of authority. It provides that the Designated Officer, after scrutiny of the report of Food Analyst shall decide as to whether the contravention is punishable with imprisonment or fine only and in the case of contravention punishable with imprisonment, he shall send his recommendations within 14 days to Commissioner of Food Safety for sanctioning prosecution. In case the contravention is punishable with fine only, he shall himself adjudicate and dispose of the case. It also provides that the Commissioner of Food Safety shall, if he so deems fit, decide within the prescribed period as per the gravity of offence, whether the matter be referred to a Court of ordinary jurisdiction in case of offences punishable with imprisonment for a term up to three years, or a Special Court in case of offences punishable with imprisonment for a term exceeding three years where such Special Court is established and in case no Special Court is established, such cases shall be tried by a Court of ordinary jurisdiction.
